To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the throughput of a web crawler is limited by the politeness constraints and not by the network bandwidth; (ii) the throughput can be improved by using a distributed architecture; (iii) the throughput is not linearly related to the number of available machines; (iv) the throughput depends on the network topology; (v) the throughput increases with the number of hosts to crawl; and (vi) the throughput decreases with the number of machines used
